items.title: Scaling Production AI with Cloud Native | CNCF Ambassador Emily Chen
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>How do we evolve infrastructure to meet the actual compute and operational demands of modern tech? CNCF Ambassador Emily Chen shares why cloud native systems are the bedrock of AI workloads, and why open source community contribution turns hype into production reliability.

The industry is moving past deploying AI for novelty. Real-world implementation requires a solid operational layer capable of orchestrating workloads, managing scaling pressures, and maintaining platform resilience. Emily highlights how active community participation gives engineers the ability to test architectures, share best practices, and contribute directly to foundational technology.

Collaborate with fellow builders on open source solutions. Register for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America:https://bit.ly/4z2FJO6

items.title: Cloud Native Live: Compliance at Scale with Kyverno - Razorpay and Nirmata
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Razorpay processes over $180 billion in payments annually and powers 80 of India’s top 100 unicorns. Operating at this scale in a regulated financial market means meeting strict Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requirements while maintaining 99.99% system availability and releasing new features quickly.

In this fireside chat, Ashwath Kumar (Head of Security at Razorpay) and Jim Bugwadia (CEO at Nirmata) share how Razorpay automated its security policies. By adopting Kyverno Razorpay moved from manual audits to continuous, automated compliance across its entire infrastructure. They will also discuss how active involvement in the CNCF community helps their business.</article>

items.title: Cloud Native Live: AI Inference with Crossplane & Modelplane
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>As open-weight models spread, platform teams are left running GPU capacity scattered across clouds, neoclouds, and on-premises clusters. Serving a model on one cluster is well covered by open source tools. The hard problems now sit above the cluster. In this Cloud Native Live session, we'll show how Crossplane handles that layer.

We'll walk through Modelplane, an Apache 2.0 project built entirely as a Crossplane configuration, with no custom controllers. You'll see how composition functions written in Python, typed schemas from the new Crossplane CLI, and Crossplane v2 namespaced composites come together to schedule models across a multi-cluster fleet. We'll also cover the upstream fixes this work drove into Crossplane. We'll show it all through live demos of Modelplane and Crossplane, from both the platform team and ML team sides.

This session is for platform engineers who want to see how far compositions and functions can go on a demanding real-world problem.</article>
